subject: Cloud Computing
title: Zero-Copy Data Sharing
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Zero-Copy Data Sharing.

hook.text: Company A wants to share data with Company B. Traditionally, that means copying it. Zero-copy says: don't.

buildup.text: Zero-copy sharing grants access to live data without duplicating it. Both parties see the same, always-current data.

discovery.text: Snowflake's data marketplace pioneered this: share datasets across organizations with no ETL, no copies, no delays.

twist.text: Zero-copy raises governance questions. Who controls the data? What happens when the sharer revokes access?

climax.text: Data sharing is becoming a product. Companies sell or exchange datasets as easily as they sell software.

punchline.text: Don't copy data to share it. Grant access to the original.

quiz.question: What is the benefit of zero-copy data sharing?
options: Both parties access the same live data without duplication or sync delays
Data is automatically deleted after being shared once
It makes all shared data publicly available on the internet

details.summary: Zero-copy data sharing lets organizations share live data without moving or copying it. Snowflake, Databricks, and BigQuery enable cross-account data access where the consumer queries data in place. This eliminates duplication, reduces cost, and ensures freshness.
details.whyItMatters: Traditional data sharing through files or API exports creates stale copies and duplication. Zero-copy sharing keeps data fresh, reduces storage costs, and simplifies governance.
takeaways: Consumers query shared data in place without copying it
Eliminates data duplication and staleness of shared copies
Snowflake's data marketplace pioneered this model

faq.question: How does zero-copy sharing work technically?
faq.answer: The data provider grants read access to specific tables or views. The consumer's compute engine queries the provider's storage directly using access controls. No data is physically moved; only metadata and permissions are shared across accounts.

faq.question: What are the security implications of zero-copy sharing?
faq.answer: Access controls must be carefully managed since consumers directly access live data. Row-level and column-level security filter sensitive data at query time. Audit logs track all access. Revoking access immediately stops data availability without needing to retrieve copies.
